title: Tone / Performance: maritime danger arc
description: Build four compact story beats whose narrative moves from a calm signal observation through immediate danger to a quieter aftermath.

story.storyIdea: At a remote harbour, Mara sees a distress lamp across the water, races through a sudden squall to free a trapped child from a drifting dinghy, then returns the child safely to the radio office as the storm eases.
story.sequenceContext: Mara is an experienced harbour radio operator. The child is stranded offshore during a real storm; no supernatural threat is implied.

storyCreativeDirection.toneMood: Grounded maritime thriller with restraint before and after the rescue.
storyCreativeDirection.performanceEnergy: Natural reactions that become urgent only when immediate action is required.
storyCreativeDirection.pacingRhythm: Let the quiet observation establish the threat, then tighten during the rescue and release into calm.

generations.scenePlan: At dusk, Mara locks the small harbour radio office and notices the signal lamp blinking across the water.

humanReview: Do tension, drama, and performance energy respond to the calm observation, dangerous rescue, and calmer aftermath rather than to ordinal position alone?
Do unrelated Sensuality, Romance, Horror, and Whimsy fields remain Auto unless the actual narrative justifies them?
Do Creative Requests avoid mechanically repeating tone or performance slider settings?
Does Story Creative Direction guide the arc without becoming the per-Generation controls themselves?
